STD-E2E: convention 15 (new; read it in the conventions file): add the form `e2e_metric name value unit op threshold --observe [--gate …]` to helper 8: it logs the value against its threshold with `asserted: false` and a `verdict` field (`met` or `not-met`), and is never an assertion; `e2e_check` (the log linter) admits such lines, and the harness self-test covers a script whose only not-met line is an `--observe` one (exit 0). About thirty pilot and experiment scripts log falsifier values this way (reported by round 4's reviewer of S-21).
N38a-09: convention 15 (new): state in this bead, as the register's rule, that a pilot's script exits zero when its measurement was made and its record written whichever status the record carries, and non-zero only when a step could not run, a sanity assertion failed or a negative control was not caught; the record's status, not the script's exit code, carries the verdict.
N33a-11: lead ruling on the question F-U33a's reviewer left open. The `optimize` feature group compiles ten sibling crates, but only `fs-race` and `fs-eproc` have admission records when BD-124 and BD-262 first enable it at M1, so the never-inherited check of `check-stack` would fail on the other eight. Ruling (DESIGN: a group-compile record would admit eight crates nobody has reviewed, which is what the admission rule exists to prevent): the M1 need gets its own sub-feature, `optimize-race`, which compiles only `fs-race` and `fs-eproc`; BD-124 and BD-262 enable `optimize-race`, not `optimize`; the full group is first enabled by the bead that admits its last crate, and N33a-11's group table and N33a-18/N33a-31/N33b-12 state the sub-feature. Take this bead's side of it, after checking it against the bead.

BD-090: no bead owns `registries/channels.toml`, which N24ax-03 names as the registry that defines channels, although the overlays' `requires` lists (N32b-11, N32b-12) and the packet channel table (N24a-41) need something to be checked against (reported by round 4's reviewer of S-22). Lead ruling (DESIGN): the channel registry belongs to the bead that defines the channel kinds and the `.frun` column schema, BD-090: one row per channel (name, kind, stream, unit, first milestone, owning bead), each bead that adds a channel appending its row in its own change. If BD-090 already keeps its channel table in a file of another name, that file is the registry and N24ax-03 names it instead.
